axiom_audit.method: #print axioms on every theorem in the file
axiom_audit.verdict: ALL SORRY-FREE. No sorryAx, no custom axioms.

theorems_banked.name: ntuple3_card_choose_le
theorems_banked.statement: NtupleCondition A 3 -> Nat.choose (A INTER Icc 1 N).ncard 3 <= 3*N + 1
theorems_banked.significance: Load-bearing counting bound. Establishes that N^(1/3) is the correct normalisation in Erdos 41: the ratio in the conjecture is BOUNDED, so the liminf is a finite number and the only open question is whether it is zero.

theorems_banked.name: ntuple3_cube_bound
theorems_banked.significance: Explicit cube form of the counting bound; gives |A cap [1,N]| <= (18N)^(1/3) + 2.

theorems_banked.name: isB3_imp_ntupleCondition
theorems_banked.significance: Faithfulness direction 1: every genuine B_3 set satisfies the corpus condition, so the corpus hypothesis class CONTAINS the true one and the corpus theorem is at least as strong as Erdos 41.

theorems_banked.name: ntupleCondition_not_isB3
theorems_banked.significance: Faithfulness direction 2: the containment is STRICT. 1+1+3 = 1+2+2 = 5 with multisets {1,1,3} != {1,2,2}. The corpus encoding is therefore not a faithful transcription of the prose statement.

theorems_banked.name: ntuple3_imp_ntuple2
theorems_banked.significance: Structural collapse. The hypothesis of the corpus theorem erdos_41 implies the hypothesis of erdos_41.variants.pairwise, which is Erdos's SOLVED theorem. Hence every A admissible for Erdos 41 already satisfies liminf |A cap [1,N]|/N^(1/2) = 0 for free. The open content of Erdos 41 is exactly the exponent gap 1/2 -> 1/3, and no argument that only re-derives the pairwise statement can close it.

not_claimed: Erdos 41 is NOT closed by this campaign.
No counterexample to either the prose statement or the corpus statement was found.
The analytic corollary 'liminf <= 18^(1/3)' (i.e. transporting ntuple3_cube_bound through Filter.liminf in the reals) was NOT formalised; it is routine but unproved here and is marked UNPROVED.
